in_sanskrit.name: विष्वनाथ
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: विश्व (Visva) - universe, नाथ (Natha) - protector, controller. So, Bishwanath means 'Lord of the Universe'.

in_hindi.name: विष्वनाथ
in_hindi.meaning: विश्व (Visva) - विज्ञान (Vijnana) - विश्वास (Vishvas) - universe, नाथ (Natha) - परिशद (Parishad) - प्रशासक (Prashasak) - परिकर्ता (Parikarta) - protector, controller, servant. So, Bishwanath means 'Lord of the Universe'.

in_tamil.name: விஷ்வநாத்
in_tamil.long_meaning: விஷ் (Viṣ) - universe, நாத் (Natha) - நல்ல விஷயம் (Nalla Visayam) - good thing, good quality, அரியவர் (Ariyan) - noble, good person. So, Bishwanath means 'Lord of the good universe' or 'Lord of the good quality universe'.

in_telugu.name: విష్శనాథ

data.spiritual_significance: The name Bishwanath holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus, symbolizing the presiding deity of the entire universe. It is often associated with the Shiva character, particularly in the Shaivite tradition, who represents the all-pervading consciousness and the supreme godhead. Bishwanath signifies the ultimate reality and is considered to be the ultimate resort for protection and salvation. Devotion to Bishwanath is believed to help attain spiritual liberation and inner peace.

historical_references.reference: The Sanskrit name 'Bishwānātha' is derived from two roots: 'Bishwa' meaning universe or all pervading, and 'Natha' meaning master or lord. This name is often associated with the Hindu deity Shiva, who is considered the master of the universe.

During the medieval period, the temple town of Puri in Odisha, India, was a major pilgrimage site for Hindus. The temple of Lord Jagannath, located in Puri, was believed to be presided over by three deities: Jagannath (Lord of the Universe), Balabhadra (Brother of Jagannath), and Subhadra (Sister of Jagannath). Lord Jagannath is also referred to as Bishwannath or Bishwanatha, highlighting his role as the master of the universe.
